what: The pedal's physical and software interface, as data: every signal that has to be present
for the thing to work, and what a fault in each one looks like from software. It exists so
`pedal-diag` can check an observation against an expectation and name the wire, rather than
printing a wall of numbers for a human to interpret.
One home per fact (docs/working-across-repos.md rule 1). The prose the rows come from:
- docs/codec-bringup-2a.md stage 4    the codec board to the 40-pin header
- docs/uart-protocol.md               the Pico to the Core host
- devices/vip/rootfs/etc/pedal/tune.conf  the CPU split and the audio interrupt
Those documents stay the explanation; this file is the form a tool can check. Change both
together, or a diagnostic will confidently name the wrong wire.

codec.board: SparkFun WM8960 Audio Codec Breakout v1.0
codec.why_no_id: The WM8960 has no device ID register: R0 is LINVOL (left input volume) and the driver writes 0x0117 into it, so a read of R0 returns a volume and never a part number. The model claimed an id of 0x8960 at register 0 until 2026-10-06, which no read could ever have produced (sound/soc/codecs/wm8960.h; bench-results/2026-10-06-codec-i2c-reads-and-the-sda-hold-time.md).
notes: The codec board carries its own 24 MHz oscillator (Y1) and MCLK is not brought out: the
codec is the I2S master and the Core host is the slave. A host that tried to master would
The I2C interface is in the DBVDD domain, fed from 3V3 on header pin 1 — so a displaced
pin 1 alone gives 'the card never appears', not just a dead oscillator.
ADCLRC is deliberately NOT wired: the Pi's I2S has one frame clock (GPIO19/DACLRC) and the
overlay (wlf,gpio-cfg ALRCGPIO + wlf,shared-lrclk) runs the ADC from DACLRC too. Wiring it
as well would put two outputs on one pin.

signals.carries: DCVDD, DBVDD and the 24 MHz oscillator (Y1)
signals.fault_symptom: no I2C at all: 0x1a NACKs, the codec never appears in the kernel log, and the board's PWR LED is dark (the LED is on 3V3)
signals.check: meter 3.3 V at the codec board's 3V3 pin, and check the lead in header pin 1 is seated

signals.carries: the onboard LDO (U3, XC6222B331MR-G) into AVDD, and SPKVDD
signals.fault_symptom: the board answers on I2C (3V3 is fine) but AVDD is dead: the card appears, the stream runs, and capture is digital silence or very low
signals.check: meter 5 V at VIN and 3.3 V at the codec's AVDD-ISO side; check the lead in header pin 2
notes: Header pin 2 also feeds the Pico's VSYS through its 1N5817 since 2026-10-05. Pins 1, 2, 3 and 5 are neighbours, so a second lead in pin 2 sits a lead's width from 3.3 V, SDA and SCL. The Pico's feed belongs on pin 4 so pin 2 keeps the codec's lead alone (plan.md 3.6).

signals.carries: I2C1 data, with 2.2 k pull-ups on the codec board
signals.fault_symptom: the codec never appears, or every address on the bus times out: a held line. A NACK at 0x1a with the rest of the bus quiet is the board not answering, which is its power or its seating
signals.check: meter SDA to 3.3 V (the pull-ups should hold it high when idle); reseat the lead in header pin 3

signals.fault_symptom: as SDA: no codec, or a bus that times out on every address
signals.check: meter SCL to 3.3 V while idle; reseat the lead in header pin 5

signals.carries: the bit clock, 3.072 MHz at 48 kHz (64 x fs)
signals.fault_symptom: capture is RUNNING and no period ever completes: 'capture timed out after 1000 ms (last state 3, ring 0 frames)'. With no bit clock the RP1's I2S RX makes no DMA requests, so nothing is ever transferred
signals.check: a lead out of header pin 12 — this is a wire, not a configuration. Twisting it loosely with the pin 39 ground lead is what the bring-up asks for

signals.carries: the frame clock, 48 kHz, and it is the one LRCLK for both directions
signals.fault_symptom: the card binds but the stream does not run cleanly, or the sample rate is wrong: one frame clock pin serves the ADC too, so losing it stops both directions

signals.carries: the recorded audio, codec to host
signals.fault_symptom: the classic: the stream runs, periods complete on time, and the capture is EXACT ZEROS. A timeout and zeros are not the same fault — no clock versus no data
signals.check: the lead in header pin 38. This is the one that was found in the wrong socket on 2026-10-04 (bench-results/2026-10-04-case-no-audio-diagnosis.md)

signals.carries: the playback audio, host to codec
signals.fault_symptom: the engine renders, the capture is healthy, and nothing comes out of the output jacks

signals.carries: the return, and it belongs beside the I2S leads
signals.fault_symptom: anything at all: a floating ground is a floating bus. It shows up as noise, intermittent enumeration or a dead codec
signals.check: both ground leads, starting with pin 6

signals.fault_symptom: wiring it as well puts two outputs on one pin: the frame clock fights and the codec misbehaves intermittently
signals.check: no lead. If one is fitted, remove it

pico_link.line: 8N1, raw, no getty on this port (the console is ttyAMA10)

enabled_by.cause: RP1's UART0 (serial@30000, header pins 8 and 10) is disabled in the stock device tree, so the pedal loads its own overlay at boot
enabled_by.why: A card rewrite on 2026-10-05 came back without it: the link was dead while the engine, the codec and everything else were fine (bench-results/2026-10-05-header-uart-disabled.md)
enabled_by.check: systemctl status pedal-uart; cat /sys/kernel/config/device-tree/overlays/*/status; then dmesg for '1f00030000.serial'

signals.to: Core host header pin 10 (GPIO15, ttyAMA0 TXD)
signals.carries: the Pico's side of the protocol: HELLO, PONG, EVENT, STATE
signals.fault_symptom: no HELLO and no frames arriving at all: frames_ok stops climbing while pedald still reports the port open
signals.check: the lead in header pin 10, at both ends

signals.from: Core host header pin 8 (GPIO14, ttyAMA0 RXD)
signals.carries: the host's side: WELCOME, PING, ACK
signals.fault_symptom: HELLO arrives and the session never comes up (no WELCOME reaches the Pico): frames_ok climbs but pedald reports session false
signals.check: the lead in header pin 8, at both ends. The firmware holds RX with a pull-up, so a floating RX invents bytes rather than going quiet

signals.fault_symptom: framing errors (frames_bad climbing) with occasional good frames: the two ends disagree about what a byte is
signals.check: the ground lead at both ends

signals.from: Core host header pin 4 (5 V), through a 1N5817
signals.carries: the Pico's power, so it survives a Core host reboot and shutdown
signals.fault_symptom: the Pico restarts with the host: its console uptime resets across a reboot. The firmware prints 'fw: up N s' every 5 s on its USB console, counting from the Pico's own reset, which is the only measurement that sees this
signals.check: plan.md 3.6 / scripts/pico-power-test: read the uptime, reboot the host, read it again. The USB-A leg was ruled out on 2026-10-05; the header leg holds

boot: fw: <version>, protocol <major>.<minor> on UART0 GP0/GP1 at 115200 baud
counters: proto: frames ok=<n> bad=<n> events lost=<n> session=<u> rig=<d> name='<s>'

notes: The console is the firmware's own account of what it has seen, which is not the same as what the host has seen: pedald's counters are the other half. Read both.

state_words.PREPARED: opened and prepared, not started: the engine is between blocks, or it is stopped
state_words.XRUN: the device is in an overrun or underrun and will not recover without a prepare

likely: the codec is not answering on I2C (see codec.signals: 3V3 first, then SDA/SCL)
the overlay did not load: check dmesg for 'wm8960 1-001a' and 'card wm8960 did not appear'
faults.check: sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/1-001a/registers — if this file exists the driver bound the codec, and the problem is later

faults.symptom: the card exists and the engine cannot open it
likely: another process holds the PCM (check the owner pid in the status file)
hw_params do not match: the engine asks for an exact period size and refuses a device that cannot give it
faults.check: compare /proc/asound/card0/pcm0p/sub0/hw_params with this file's audio block, field by field

cpu.source: /etc/pedal/tune.conf, and /usr/local/sbin/pedal-tune check is the authority on whether it is in force

notes: The active trips are where the firmware starts pulling the clock back, so the number that matters is the distance to 50 C, not the 110 C critical trip.

engine.wire: a 4-byte little-endian length prefix then one JSON object, both directions; the token goes at the TOP LEVEL of engine.hello, and the id is a string

levels.units: dBFS, one decimal; the floor is the sentinel for digital silence
notes: Added by this plan: namchain has no audio-level measurement at all as of b9ca368. Until it
lands, pedal-diag reports levels as unavailable and says so in one line rather than
printing zeros that look like silence.

attached_aids.name: Raspberry Pi Debug Probe

ports.A: USB, to whatever host is looking
ports.D: SWD (JST-SH), to the Pico's debug pads
ports.U: UART (3-pin), to whichever serial line is being watched

attached_aids.usb_host: Port A goes to the machine that runs the tooling, which by design is the Mac: decided 2026-09-29, the probe stays on the Pico while the Core host's console is set up on its 3-pin header (docs/vip-image.md). Its USB is on the pedal host only in the bench case where the pedal host is itself the debugger.

watches.target: the Pico's link UART (probe RX <- GP0/pin 1, GND <-> pin 3)
watches.what_it_looks_like: protocol frames: every frame starts a5 5a, and the firmware sends HELLO about once a second whether or not the Core host answers

watches.target: the Core host's own console on its 3-pin debug header (ttyAMA10, 115200)
watches.what_it_looks_like: kernel and getty text; silent while the host is up and idle, and the bootloader's first line arrives only at a power-on
nothing readable: SWD needs a debugger on the other end, so its traffic cannot be seen passively

may_be_attached_to: the Pico's UART (probe RX yellow <- GP0/pin 1, probe TX orange -> GP1/pin 2, GND black <-> pin 3) — what firmware/tools/echo-test.py and firmware/tools/protocol-test.py assume
the Core host's 3-pin debug header (the Pi 5's console, ttyAMA10, and the bootloader's own output with BOOT_UART=1) — what tools/measure-boot.py assumes
the Mac rather than the pedal
notes: Its absence is never a fault: it is a bench aid, and the Pico's console is also reachable over its own USB (/dev/ttyACM0 on the Core host).

A report gathered on the pedal host cannot see the operator's machine, so 'no Debug Probe' on the pedal is the expected state and not news: the tool says which machines it looked at, and reads the operator's own USB itself.
The D port cannot be read without halting the target, so nothing continuous uses it: pedal-diag --probe only, and never while the engine is playing.
The probe's UART cannot be shared: if it already carries a getty's line, rendering writes nothing to it.

known_fault_seeds.symptom: every read of the codec fails while writes are clean: i2cget -f -y 1 0x1a <reg> w returns 'Error: Read failed', and dmesg carries i2c_dw_handle_tx_abort: lost arbitration and SDA stuck at low
known_fault_seeds.discriminator: a read of an unused address (0x20) completes with a plain NAK and no abort, and a write through the driver (amixer, same value plus one step) succeeds with no abort either — so the bus and the codec are both alive and only this codec's read aborts
known_fault_seeds.meaning: the driver's register file is a cache because the controller cannot complete a read from this codec, not because anything is missing from userspace. i2c-tools is installed and issues the codec's own protocol; i2c-sda-hold-time-ns at 300, 1000 and 3000 ns changes nothing; and a single-message read with no repeated start fails the same way, so it is not the restart. Suspect the RP1 controller's read path or the codec's read protocol
known_fault_seeds.check: a second I2C device with a known ID register on the same bus (reads failing on it too means the controller) or a scope on SDA and SCL during one read. Do NOT set a large i2c-sda-hold-time-ns: 10 us is a whole bit period at 100 kHz and wedged the controller holding SDA low, which needed a reboot (the node has no scl-gpios/sda-gpios, so i2c_recover_bus() is a no-op)

known_fault_seeds.symptom: pedal-codec fails with 'card wm8960 did not appear'; /proc/asound/cards is empty
known_fault_seeds.discriminator: the driver's own reset write to 0x1a returns -121 (EREMOTEIO, a NACK) rather than -110 (ETIMEDOUT, the controller's timeout)
known_fault_seeds.meaning: a NACK is the Pi driving the bus and being told 'nobody here' — the board is not answering. A timeout is a held line, which is a short or a crossed lead. They have different fixes and the error number is the whole difference
known_fault_seeds.check: the board's supplies and its I2C are four adjacent header pins (1, 2, 3, 5). Check those leads and the board's seating in its socket strips first — the I2C interface is in the DBVDD domain, fed from 3V3 on pin 1, so a displaced pin 1 alone gives this symptom

known_fault_seeds.symptom: capture timed out after 1000 ms (last state 3, ring 0 frames)
known_fault_seeds.meaning: PCM RUNNING and no frames: with no bit clock the RP1's I2S RX makes no DMA requests, so no period ever completes
known_fault_seeds.check: BCLK — the lead in header pin 12

known_fault_seeds.symptom: the capture completes on time and is exact zeros
known_fault_seeds.meaning: clock present, data absent: ADAT (ADCDAT) in the wrong socket on the codec board
known_fault_seeds.check: the lead in header pin 38. Zeros and a timeout are not the same fault

known_fault_seeds.symptom: playback is rendering and one output jack is silent
known_fault_seeds.meaning: the rig leaves on channel 0 = HPL, so the interface's cable belongs in OUT L until a chain's output_channel is bound
known_fault_seeds.check: which jack the cable is in, and the chain's output_channel in the running rig

known_fault_seeds.symptom: the Pico appears to be alive and re-sends HELLO after a reboot, which a HELLO cannot distinguish from a restart
known_fault_seeds.meaning: the Pico re-sends HELLO after a 1 s link timeout, restart or not, so a HELLO is not evidence of power. Only the Pico's own uptime is
known_fault_seeds.check: scripts/pico-power-test --leg read, before and after: the counter runs from the Pico's reset

cannot_be_seen_from_software: Which socket a lead is in, physically. The tool narrows the fault to a signal and names the pin; a meter or a photo closes it.
A lead that is fitted but making poor contact: intermittent, so it shows as noise, occasional framing errors or an occasional device loss rather than a clean absence.
An I2S line that is present and clocking but at the wrong logic level: it looks like data, and only a scope sees it.
Whether the case is the aluminium one, whether a panel part is fitted, and the state of anything not yet built (display, footswitches, MIDI, expression, relay).
Anything about the analogue side beyond the codec: the input buffer's gain switch, the output stage, the star ground.
